chunks: And in the narration of Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
"Whoever withholds a qīrāṭ of zakat is not a believer nor a Muslim, and this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:"
"Until, when death comes to one of them, he says: My Lord, send me back. So that I may do righteousness in that which I left behind."
And in another narration: "And no salat (prayer) is accepted from him."

key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: zakat (alms-tax), the obligatory financial due owed from wealth
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ: death, the moment when regret over neglected duty becomes manifest
key_terms.بِمُؤْمِنٍ: a believer, here meaning one whose faith is negated by this act
key_terms.صَالِحًا: righteous deed, referring to the good action the person failed to perform
key_terms.صَلَاةٌ: salat (prayer), whose acceptance is denied in the other narration
key_terms.قِيرَاطًا: a very small measured amount, showing that even slight withholding of zakat is serious
key_terms.مُسْلِمٍ: a Muslim, here used to emphasize the severity of refusing zakat

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about withholding zakat?
ai.summary: This hadith strongly condemns withholding zakat, presenting it as a grave violation that contradicts true faith and Islam. It links refusal to pay zakat with the Qur’anic scene of regret at death, when a person wishes to return and perform the neglected righteous deeds. Another report adds that such a person's salat (prayer) is not accepted.
